summary.authors: Hongji Huang, Yiwei Song, Jie Yang, Guan Gui, Fumiyuki Adachi

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper addresses the high computational complexity and suboptimal performance of existing hybrid precoding schemes in millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive MIMO systems. The authors propose a novel framework that integrates deep learning (DNN) to optimize the selection of hybrid precoders. By treating the precoder selection as a mapping relation within a deep neural network, the study aims to exploit the spatial sparsity of mmWave channels more effectively than traditional mathematical methods like Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) or Geometric Mean Decomposition (GMD). The system model utilizes a Saleh-Valenzuela channel model with a uniform linear array at the base station. Extensive simulations were conducted using the Keras framework with a carrier frequency of 28 GHz and 3 non-line-of-sight components. The results demonstrate that the proposed DNN-based approach significantly outperforms conventional schemes in terms of Bit Error Ratio (BER) and spectrum efficiency. Furthermore, the method achieves superior convergence speed, requiring approximately half the iterations of analog precoding schemes to reach the Mean Square Error (MSE) target. The study concludes that deep learning offers a robust solution for reducing hardware complexity while enhancing system throughput in next-generation communications.

Research Context
Wireless data traffic is predicted to improve 1000-fold by the year 2020. Millimeter wave (mmWave) massive MIMO is an emerging solution for next generation. Existing hybrid precoding schemes have high computational complexity. Traditional schemes fail to fully exploit the spatial information. Previous works are based on conventional mathematical means such as SVD. Traditional methods are inadequate to leverage the structural characteristics.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study investigates a framework integrating deep learning into hybrid precoding. The hypothesis is that a DNN can minimize the bit error ratio (BER). It is hypothesized that the DNN approach will enhance spectrum efficiency. The proposed scheme is expected to achieve better performance compared with conventional schemes. The method should substantially reduce the required computational complexity. Deep learning is an excellent tool to deal with complex non-convex problems.

Methodological Details
The study considers a typical mmWave massive MIMO system. The base station has a uniform linear array of Nt antennas. The user has Nr received antennas. The BS sends Ns independent data streams to the user. The Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model is introduced. The carrier frequency is given as 28 GHz. The number of non-line-of-sight components is P = 3. The analog precoder is high-dimensional and the digital precoder is low-dimensional. All elements of DA and BA are supposed to meet the requirement as |{DA}i,j| = 1/sqrt(Nt). The study employs a state-of-the-art DNN to construct a novel precoding framework.

Procedures And Architectures
The proposed DNN framework is exhibited in Fig. 1. The input layer is a fully connected layer with 128 units. The next two hidden layers comprise 400 units and 256 units. A noise layer is consisted of 200 units for mixing distortion. The remaining two hidden layers have 128 units and 64 units. The ReLU function is introduced as the activation function of the input layer and the hidden layers. A special activation is designed as f(s) = min(max(s, 0), Ns) for the output layer. The GMD method is adopted to decompose the complex mmWave massive MIMO channel matrix. The stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm with momentum is employed. The network has been trained for 45000 iterations in the simulation. Keras is used to construct and process the DNN framework.

Key Results
The deep-learning-based method outperforms the conventional schemes. The performance improvement is more apparent between the deep-learning-based strategy and conventional methods. The proposed mmWave massive MIMO strategy is superior to the fully GMD-based digital precoding mean. The performance of the deep-learning-based strategy degrades with increasing batch size in terms of BER. Too small batch size will lead to unstable convergence. The performance of hybrid precoding is optimized by adopting a lower learning rate. The spectrum efficiency is improving as the SNR increases in all the schemes. The proposed hybrid precoding scheme outperforms other strategies. The performance gap of the deep learning based scheme and that of other approaches is becoming larger. The proposed deep learning based scheme and the sparse precoding method both convert at around 11 iterations. The analog precoding scheme requires about 22 iterations. The MSE performance of the proposed deep learning based scheme is superior than that of other means.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The excellent representation ability of deep learning contributes to the performance improvement. The DNN utilizes the structural information and can approach each iteration of the algorithm. The existing non-convex optimization in hybrid precoding can be solved with the aid of deep learning. The proposed approach realizes superior performance in terms of the hybrid precoding accuracy and conversion. Deep learning can facilitate the hybrid precoding because of its great recognition and mapping abilities. Another promising direction is to apply deep learning in the channel feedback issue.

Contradictions And Limitations
The performance of the deep-learning-based strategy degrades with increasing batch size. Too small batch size will lead to unstable convergence. A larger learning rate causes a higher validation error. Slower convergence behavior will be induced by using a lower learning rate. How to select the best learning rate is an open issue in the proposed framework. The study assumes that the BS has no information on all the communication links.

Claims
The DNN-based approach minimizes the bit error ratio and enhances spectrum efficiency. The deep-learning-based method outperforms the conventional schemes. The proposed hybrid precoding scheme outperforms other strategies. The performance degrades with increasing batch size. Deep learning can facilitate the hybrid precoding because of its great recognition and mapping abilities.
The proposed method substantially reduces the required computational complexity. The complexity of the deep-learning-based method is only O(L2NsN2t). The proposed deep learning based scheme and the sparse precoding method both convert at around 11 iterations. Slower convergence behavior will be induced by using a lower learning rate. This method lowers the computational complexity.

Data And Code Availability
Keras is used to construct and process the DNN framework.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The performance is evaluated with different learning rates and various batch sizes. The robustness and stability are explored by investigating the relationship between MSE and iterations. The proposed deep learning based scheme and the sparse precoding method both convert at around 11 iterations.

Key Figures Tables
Fig. 1 shows the DNN architecture in the proposed scheme. TABLE I illustrates the computational complexity of several precoding schemes. Fig. 2 shows BER versus SNR comparing the proposed method with conventional schemes. Fig. 3 shows BER versus SNR with various batch sizes. Fig. 4 presents the BER versus SNR with various learning rates. Fig. 5 shows spectrum efficiency versus SNR for different schemes. Fig. 6 shows MSE versus iterations for the deep learning-based method.

Three Takeaways
The core contribution is a deep-learning-enabled mmWave massive MIMO framework for effective hybrid precoding. The strongest evidence is that the proposed scheme outperforms other strategies in spectrum efficiency and converges faster. The future path involves applying deep learning in the channel feedback issue to alleviate codebook size issues.
